items.focus: Be ready to describe the FastAPI endpoints you built for CV uploads: HTTP methods, request/response handling, file validation logic and how you extracted document text with Python. Link this to the job requirement to develop Python applications and FastAPI endpoints.
items.title: Explaining your FastAPI endpoints and file validation pipeline

Describe file validation: type, size, and error handling.
Explain text extraction using Python libraries and any challenges.
Summarise how you tested the endpoint with sample documents.
items.question: Can you walk me through the FastAPI endpoints you implemented for CV uploads? What HTTP methods did you use, how did you validate files, and how did you extract text?

items.focus: Prepare to discuss how you built the Vue portfolio with TypeScript, including component structure, type safety and integration with the FastAPI backend. This addresses the requirement to build Vue and TypeScript interfaces.
items.title: Describing your Vue and TypeScript interface work
outline: Outline the Vue component architecture and TypeScript usage.
Explain API calls to FastAPI endpoints and data handling.

items.focus: Expand on how you tested the application with sample documents. Be ready to specify the types of tests (unit, integration) and any frameworks used, even if informal. This supports the requirement to validate files and test applications.
items.title: Discussing your testing approach and frameworks
outline: Clarify whether tests were manual or automated.
Name any frameworks or tools used (e.g. pytest, Jest).
Describe test cases for file validation and text extraction.
Explain how you handled edge cases and errors.
items.question: What types of tests did you write for your application, and did you use any testing frameworks?

items.focus: The job description lists PostgreSQL as useful, but your CV does not evidence it. Prepare to acknowledge this gap and describe any transferable database knowledge or your plan to learn PostgreSQL. Do not fabricate experience.
items.title: Addressing PostgreSQL familiarity honestly
outline: State clearly whether you have used PostgreSQL or other databases.
If you have transferable skills, describe them briefly.
Outline a concrete plan to learn PostgreSQL basics.
Relate database concepts to your current project (e.g. storing uploads).
items.question: The role mentions PostgreSQL familiarity. What experience do you have with databases, and how would you approach learning PostgreSQL?

items.focus: Frame your CV upload project as relevant to AI application engineering: document processing, validation and potential integration with AI models. This helps align your experience with the role's broader context.
items.title: Connecting your project to AI application engineering
outline: Summarise the project's data flow from upload to text extraction.
Suggest how extracted text could feed into an AI model.
Discuss potential improvements for scalability or accuracy.
Show awareness of ethical and validation concerns.
items.question: How does your CV upload project relate to AI application engineering, and how would you extend it to incorporate AI?

preparation.summary: Your CV already evidences the core requirements for this AI Application Engineer role: Python, FastAPI, Vue, TypeScript, file validation and testing. The main gap is PostgreSQL, which the job description lists as useful rather than essential. Use this plan to deepen your project narratives, prepare for technical questions on your existing work, and address the database gap honestly. Focus on explaining design decisions, testing approaches and how you would extend your current project. Do not claim experience you do not have; instead, show willingness to learn PostgreSQL and related concepts.
